summary: Scope: the one added line, baselines/review.txt:15 (rounds:M4.38). It is well-formed for the gate (key rounds:M4.38 as the first whitespace field, non-space reason after it, ADDED in a staged baselines/review.txt), and it does what review.md rule two-round-cap asks: it says why these bytes cannot be split rather than pleading the round count. Its checkable facts hold against my own artifacts. 17 doc insertions across three docs files and no code: measured, 1+13+3. Round 1 = M4.36's shared-root-cause defect: matches R1 at hash 2853f985. Round 2 = the latch recipe pinning nothing, measured both ways: matches R2-2 and test-reviewer T3 at 9a50b5d0, and T3 did measure CountDownLatch surviving and Semaphore.acquireUninterruptibly killing. Round 3 = putIfMatch opens no channel and completes with the flag set, only putIfAbsent (the acquire path) throws, both reviewers measured independently: matches M4.38-R3-1 and T1 at a6f08958, and I re-measured it myself at b699a7d0. Round 4 = pass both roles, minors all prose, none fixed: matches b699a7d0, and the staged delta since then is only this line, so 'rather than fixed' is true of the bytes. The three clause-attachment errors resolve to R2 (round 1), M4.38-R3-2 and M4.38-R3-1's secondary, two of them inside sentences written to fix the previous one. The entry claims no convergence and names its own drafting as the cause; it does not blame the reviewers for what it adopted from them. Three minors, all about how the entry accounts for the rounds, none blocking; fixing any of them moves the hash and buys the round this line exists to argue for.

findings.title: 'ROUNDS 2 AND 3 WERE THE SAME ERROR TWICE' undercounts: it happened a third time, the third instance is still live in the tree, and the entry files it under the wrong cause
findings.failure_scenario: The entry names its recurring error precisely -- 'I promoted a reviewer's UNMEASURED structural reasoning into a row as flat fact' -- and closes the count at two. The round-4 minor it does acknowledge is a third instance of exactly that error, not of the clause-attachment family it is filed under. Round 3's test-reviewer wrote, as unmeasured structural reasoning in finding T2 (a6f08958): 'A plain CountDownLatch.await() would work perfectly well there.' The author promoted it into M4.36 as flat fact -- 'nothing interrupts its committer, and a latch would serve there' (backlog-notes.md, M4.36) -- and both round-4 reviewers found it false (M4.38-R4-1 and T1 at b699a7d0: the spin waits for a transition that happens inside submit() while the caller is already blocked in commit(), so no latch can be tripped at that instant, which the M4.7 done row added by this same commit states in its own words). The entry instead attributes it to sentence length: 'the remedy applied was shorter sentences, and round 4 shows it was only partly effective, since "a latch would serve there" is still false'. Consequence: this file is the durable record of what the escape bought, and the lesson it records is 'I did this twice and then stopped', when the tree ships a live third instance in a todo row. A future session reading rule two-round-cap's growing-list warning and then this entry gets a diagnosis that has already been falsified by the round it summarises, and the remedy it will copy is 'write shorter sentences' rather than 'measure a reviewer's hypothesis before writing it down as fact'.

findings.title: 'four minors' is a per-role count offered as a total, in the one commit whose done-row was already corrected for asserting a minor count
findings.failure_scenario: 'Round 4 passed both roles with four minors, all prose'. Both roles returned four each at b699a7d0 -- reviewer M4.38-R4-1..4 and test-reviewer T1..T4 -- and three pairs are the same defect seen twice (latch-would-serve-there, backslash-escaped quotes, the same measurement carried with two different ranges). The deduped set is FIVE: the test-reviewer's T2 ('M4.35's leading INTERLEAVING paragraph, and its "Either way", are stale after the correction that follows them') has no production twin, and the production reviewer's M4.38-R4-3 ('Neither backend that exists has it' is false under its nearest antecedent) has no test twin. Since rule minors-land makes the commit body the only place these survive and rule minors-at-milestone harvests from there, an author transcribing the entry's 'four' drops one of the five -- most likely T2, the one with no counterpart to remind anyone it existed. This is the same defect the M4.38 done-row in this very commit records having been corrected for: 'a first draft asserted "the five minors" and review showed the count was both wrong and a completeness claim the rows do not meet'. Naming what round 4 found, as the done-row now names what it files, costs the same number of words and cannot go stale.

findings.title: The entry's round ordinals do not reconcile with review_rounds.py, because round 1 was recorded under --task M4.35 -- and that stray round now sits on a row this commit files as todo
findings.failure_scenario: The entry narrates Round 1 through Round 4. `python3 scripts/review_rounds.py --for-task M4.38` returns 3, and the round-1 verdicts the entry describes (hash 2853f985: R1 the M4.36 shared-root-cause defect, R2 the M4.35 clause attachment, R3 'the commit is filed under M4.35, an ID whose row describes a production fix this diff does not make') are recorded under `--task M4.35`, which is why the packet for this round says 'round 4' where the entry says round 5's worth of history. Two consequences, neither of which the entry discloses in the one clause it would take. (a) A reader auditing this argument against the tool the same file elsewhere insists on -- M0.53's entry: 'the count is left to review_rounds.py, because a count carried by hand in prose is stale' -- finds the ordinals and the artifacts off by one and cannot tell which is wrong. (b) The worse one: M4.35 is a row THIS COMMIT files as todo, and it already carries one distinct reviewed hash. The first review of the real M4.35 fix will therefore be reported as round 2 of 2, and its second round will trip the cap and demand its own argued exception for a commit that has genuinely been reviewed once. That is a mis-armed gate on a future task, created by this commit's own round 1 and made checkable by the ordinals this line introduces.
